items.title: Six More Pairs: Teacher and Student, Shame and Its Absence, and What Ripens Insight

items.zh: 又有二種師及弟子教授教誡相違之法。謂諸弟子不能堪忍教誨語言；及師倒見，習行邪行。與此相違，當知即是白品二法。又有二法，甚能違越世出世間正行境界。謂於自非法增上所生不可愛果無有顧慮，於所作罪無有羞恥；及於現法他所殺縛衰退等事無有顧慮，於所作罪無有羞恥。與此相違，當知即是白品二法。又有二種無倒建立，能令行者少用功力，住於梵行，終不唐捐。一、正立學處。若有違越，便獲大罪；若不違越、便生大福。二、正立出離。令違越者速復出離。又有二法，能令作者得自他利。一、居遠離者，心常安定現法樂住；二、居憒閙者，有來求法，時時為說，能令正法相續久住。又有二法，能令有情內正作意、外聞他音二因緣故，於現法中入諦現觀，或令當來諸根成熟。一、於因所生法，正通達因，二、於如來所說所有甚深相似甚深空相應經，一切緣性及諸緣起，隨順作意數數思惟。又有二法，能令根熟補特伽羅速證通慧。一、於教授教誡遠離諂誑；二、厭離為先，身語意行離諸調戲。
items.en: There are also two ways teacher and disciple can run contrary to right instruction and admonition: the disciple's inability to bear the words of correction; and the teacher's own inverted views and unwholesome conduct. The reverse of these should be known as the corresponding two bright phenomena. There are also two things that gravely transgress the domain of both worldly and supramundane right conduct: having no regard for the disagreeable results one's own wrongdoing will produce, and no shame for the offence committed; and having no regard, in this very life, for being killed, bound, or brought to ruin by others because of it, and no shame for the offence committed. There are also two undistorted establishments that let a practitioner dwell in the pure life with little exertion and never in vain: rightly establishing the precepts — transgression incurring great fault, non-transgression yielding great merit; and rightly establishing the means of release — enabling one who has transgressed to swiftly be released from it again. There are also two things that let one who practises them attain benefit for both self and others: dwelling in seclusion, the mind constantly settled and abiding in the ease of the present life; and dwelling amid the crowd, teaching those who come seeking the Dharma from time to time, so that the true teaching continues long in the world. There are also two things that, through the two conditions of correct inner attention and hearing the voice of another from without, bring a being, in this very life, to direct realisation of the truths, or else bring their faculties to ripeness in a future life. There are also two things that bring one whose faculties have ripened swiftly to realise penetrating wisdom: freedom from flattery and deceit towards instruction and admonition; and, aversion coming first, freeing bodily, verbal, and mental conduct from all frivolity.

items.title: Living Well Together: Patience, Fellowship, Confession, and the Discipline of Ordinary Retreat

items.zh: 又有二法，令居一處同梵行者，展轉皆得安樂而住。一者、堪忍他所逼惱，二者、自不逼惱於他。又有二法，令居一處同梵行者，未生違諍遮令不生，其已生者速令止息，無鬪、無訟、無諍、無競。一者、展轉互起慈心，二者、平等受用財法。又有二法，速令心住，得三摩地清淨梵行。一者、憶持久遠所作、所說增上力故，若有所犯，如法悔除；若無所犯，便生歡喜；晝夜隨學，甞無懈廢。二者、於身語意一切事業能正了知增上力故，於諸過失終無違犯。由此因緣，亦無憂悔，隨生歡喜，廣說乃至解脫智見。又有二法，能越眾苦。謂能超越諸惡趣苦，及能超越生死大苦。一者、深見現法、當來諸過患故，遠離惡行；二者、心常安定，精勤修習菩提分法。又有二法，能令修斷居遠離者得安樂住。一者、於諸境界不生雜染，無惡尋伺擾亂其心；二者、凡所噉食，要為利益，稱量消化，能隨順斷，令身調適。又有二法，令修善品諸苾芻等時無虛度。一者、於諸根境正勤方便研究法相；二者、知時知量，少習睡眠。
items.en: There are also two things that let those dwelling together in the pure life all abide, mutually, at ease: bearing with what others inflict, and not oneself inflicting on others. There are also two things that prevent unarisen discord among those dwelling together in the pure life and swiftly quell what has already arisen, so that there is no strife, no litigation, no contention, no rivalry: mutually arousing loving-kindness towards one another, and sharing wealth and Dharma equally. There are also two things that swiftly settle the mind and yield the pure life of concentration: remembering, with sustained force, what has long been done and said — confessing as the Dharma prescribes what has been transgressed, rejoicing where nothing has been transgressed, applying oneself day and night without ever slackening; and rightly comprehending, with sustained force, every deed of body, speech, and mind, so that faults are never committed at all. There are also two things that let one transcend the multitude of sufferings — transcending the sufferings of the lower destinies, and transcending the great suffering of saṃsāra itself: seeing deeply the faults, present and future, [of wrongdoing], and thereby forsaking unwholesome conduct; and a mind constantly settled, diligently cultivating the factors of enlightenment. There are also two things that let one practising severance in seclusion dwell at ease: not generating defilement towards any sense-object, with no unwholesome thought or deliberation disturbing the mind; and eating, whatever is eaten, strictly for its benefit, in measured and digestible amount, conducive to severance, keeping the body well regulated. There are also two things that let monks practising wholesome conduct never pass their time in vain: applying diligent effort to investigating the characteristics of phenomena through the faculties and their objects; and knowing the proper time and measure, sleeping little.

items.title: The Final Six Pairs: Faith and Wrong View, Ripening Towards Realisation, and an Arhat's Own Certainty — the Source Text Concludes

items.zh: 又有二法，能壞增上心學、慧學。一者、建立邪學，違越正學，及懷猶豫；二者、增益、損減邪見決定。與此相違，當知即是白品二法。又有二法，能令已集菩提資糧未入現觀補特伽羅速入現觀。一者、思惟現在、過去自他衰盛，二者、勤修諦行所攝無倒作意。又有二法，令觀行者最極究竟離垢梵行速得圓滿。一者、修諦現觀；二者、於後離欲方便勤修，於諸等至無有愛味，離諸障難。又有二法，令觀行者速能引發世出世間一切勝德。一者、九相住心；二者、由六種事、以正定心思擇諸法。如聲聞地當廣分別。又觀行者有二種淨，謂作意淨及所依淨。於三世中遠離愚癡，智清淨故，名作意淨；遠離三界諸煩惱品麁重法故，名所依淨。又有二法，心善解脫諸阿羅漢內自所證。一者、於現法中苦因永盡；二者、由此為先，當來世苦畢竟不生。
items.en: There are also two things that destroy the higher training in concentration and the higher training in wisdom: establishing a wrong training, transgressing the right one, and harbouring doubt; and being fixed in a view that either superimposes or negates. The reverse of these should be known as the corresponding two bright phenomena. There are also two things that swiftly bring one who has already gathered the provisions for enlightenment but not yet entered direct realisation to enter it: reflecting on the decline and flourishing, in past and present, of oneself and others; and diligently cultivating the undistorted attention comprised within contemplating the truths. There are also two things that swiftly bring the utterly final, stainless pure life of one who contemplates to complete fulfilment: cultivating direct realisation of the truths; and, thereafter, diligently applying the means to freedom from desire, savouring none of the meditative attainments, and being free of every obstruction. There are also two things that swiftly elicit every excellent quality, worldly and supramundane, in one who contemplates: the nine ways of settling the mind; and, through six matters, investigating phenomena with a rightly concentrated mind — as will be broadly explained in the Śrāvaka Ground. Those who contemplate also have two kinds of purity: the purity of attention, and the purity of the basis. Being free, throughout the three times, of delusion, wisdom thereby purified, is called the purity of attention; being free of the coarse, heavy phenomena of affliction belonging to the three realms is called the purity of the basis. There are also two things directly realised within themselves by arhats whose minds are well liberated: in this very life, the causes of suffering are permanently exhausted; and, this being so, in future lives suffering will, in the end, never again arise.

blocks.text: The last reading of fascicle 13 completes inner wisdom with paired topics about community life: teacher and student, shame and shamelessness, patience, fellowship, confession, and the rains retreat. It ends with faith and wrong view, and with an arhat's certainty that birth is ended. It is a fitting close to the first thirteen fascicles: the most sophisticated analysis ends in how to live together.

The fourth aspect of inner wisdom lists pairs of topics. Teacher and student come first. A good teacher teaches what is true, at the right time, for the student's benefit; a good student listens attentively (Day 20's "attentive ear") and asks. Shame and its absence follow, and the conditions that ripen insight.

Patience; fellowship; confession; and the discipline of the rains retreat. These are monastic topics, but their principles apply to any community of practice: bear with others' faults, keep common rules, admit one's own faults openly, and periodically gather for focused practice.

Confession here is not self-punishment. As Master Cháng Bǎi said on Day 41: "If you did wrong and have repented, repentance purifies; don't dwell on it." The point is to restore trust and the ability to practise.
Faith and wrong view are paired: the one opens the path, the other closes it (Days 58, 63). Then, ripening towards realisation: the stages by which a practitioner matures.

The final pair: an arhat's own knowledge of liberation, expressed in the classical words, "birth is ended, the holy life fulfilled, what had to be done is done, there is no more of this." This is the "knowledge of exhaustion" and "knowledge of non-arising" of Day 92: not a hope, but a certainty one can verify in oneself.
Three fascicles of meditation and its vocabulary:

items: **The sixth stage**, meditative absorption: the four dhyānas, eight liberations, masteries, totalities, the three gateways of liberation, the immeasurables, and the attainments without perception and of cessation; the hindrances and their remedies; attention and its forty kinds; the object and its thirty-two marks; and the practical wisdom of how to enter, stay, emerge, and adjust.
**The seventh to ninth stages**, briefly: non-equipoise, and the states with and without mind, ending in the claim that only final nirvāṇa is truly "without mind".
**The tenth stage** begun: what a practitioner must hear and learn, summarised as the five sciences and Yogācāra's core vocabulary.

blocks.text: From fascicle 14, the tenth stage continues with the other four sciences (medicine, logic, linguistics, and the practical arts), and then the stages of reflection and cultivation follow.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, in what three ways do beings continue living, and by what power?
options: day by day by food; for a lifetime by the life-force; through wholesome conduct and agreeable rebirth by diligence in good dharmas
quiz.why: "Continuing day by day, continuing for the span of a lifetime, and continuing on through the mutual perpetuation of wholesome conduct and agreeable rebirth. The first is by the power of food; the second, by the power of the life-force; the third, by the power of diligence in wholesome phenomena." Venerable Miào Jìng: an engineer's diligence is only "similar" diligence.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are "darkness" and "speech"?
options: darkness is ignorance and doubt; speech is the Tathāgata's twelve divisions of teaching
quiz.why: "What is darkness? Ignorance and doubt. What is speech? The Tathāgata's twelve divisions of teaching are called speech." Venerable Miào Jìng: it takes some intelligence to doubt; with more wisdom, doubt ends.

quiz.q: Of the Three Jewels, does Venerable Miào Jìng say the verbal Dharma counts as a "jewel"?
options: words are the expedient jewel; the true jewel is nirvāṇa — only the uncontaminated path is truly precious
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "This is the expedient Dharma-jewel … the true Dharma-jewel is nirvāṇa." "'Jewel' means especially precious — only the uncontaminated noble path can be called a jewel!" Master Cháng Bǎi cites the *Ratnagotravibhāga*'s six senses of "jewel."

quiz.q: Among the five aspects of great enlightenment is "return." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain it?
options: when all beings with affinity have been saved, entering nirvāṇa — like Śākyamuni, a provisional "return"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "When all beings with affinity are saved, one enters nirvāṇa — like Śākyamuni; that is a provisional 'return.'" The text: by way of nature, capability, means, activity, and return.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain 摩怛履迦 (mātṛkā)?
options: called "mother," the mother of wisdom, also "treatise" — through it many principles are understood
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Third, mātṛkā is called 'the root mother,' the mother of wisdom, also called treatise; relying on treatises one understands many principles." Sūtra is scripture that accords with reality.
